findings.note: The note half of the owner's answer, authored in the SAME batch as its src half (src/rules/featGrants.ts HAND_AUTHORED_GRANTS 'armor-in-earth', armorFamiliarity.mirrorBest over both granted items) and never before it: the sheet now works the rank out, so the sentence telling the player to set it by hand is the only thing that changes. The whole create value is re-emitted because a create row's own post-check compares the shipped record against the create value. items/armor-in-earth-heavy takes NO row: its note never carried that sentence and the medium wording was not mirrored onto it.

value.name: Armor in Earth
value.description: Stone encases you like armor, created by the Armor in Earth impulse. It is medium armor but uses your highest armor proficiency.
value.note: Created by the Armor in Earth impulse and lasts 10 minutes (Dismissible; using the impulse again ends any existing one). It is medium armor but uses your highest armor proficiency, which your sheet works out for you. You gain its armor specialization effect. Any bonuses, runes and magical abilities of your actual armor are suppressed, and any runes that could apply to the stone armor are replicated onto it.

backfillRows.why: feat-4221 "The stone armor is medium armor but uses your highest armor proficiency." The borrowing is computed now (featGrants.ts armorFamiliarity.mirrorBest -> Proficiencies.armorOverrides, read at derive.ts:2037), so the instruction to set it by hand is wrong. CLOSER CORRECTION (batch 037 apply post-check): a corrected CREATE cannot reach an existing record — applyBackfill never overwrites one — so this row alone left the old note shipped and the post-check demanded a full regeneration. Two changes, neither of which needs `npm run data`: (a) `aonOrigin: "authored"` is restored to the create value, because the SHIPPED record carries it and the post-check compares the two whole records, so the row could never have matched without it (12 other create rows in the overlay carry it the same way); (b) the one field that actually changes, `note`, is emitted as a FIELD row below, which applyBackfill does apply to an existing record. Pre-check (1b) allows a field row beside a create row exactly when it lands after it and says byte-for-byte what the create row says, which it does.
